title: The Merino-Welsh conjecture for sparse and dense graphs

definitions.name: x2611_15008_components
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_15008_components {V E : Type*} (G : Graph V E) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card G.toSimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent
definitions.notes: Number of connected components, including isolated vertices, of Mathlib’s multigraph. Passing to toSimpleGraph discards loops and repeated adjacency only for connectivity; the vertex set is exactly G.vertexSet.

definitions.name: x2611_15008_contract
definitions.notes: Contraction of S: identify vertices by the equivalence relation generated by the endpoints of edges in S, use Graph.map to retain loops and distinct edge identities, then delete S. This implements the contraction convention in Section 2.

definitions.name: x2611_15008_bridge
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_15008_bridge {V E : Type*} (G : Graph V E) (e : E) : Prop :=
  e ∈ G.edgeSet ∧ x2611_15008_components G < x2611_15008_components (G.deleteEdges {e})
definitions.notes: An edge of G whose deletion increases the number of connected components, counting isolated vertices, exactly as defined in Section 2. Used only with finite graphs.

definitions.name: x2611_15008_parallelClass
definitions.lean:
def x2611_15008_parallelClass {V E : Type*} (G : Graph V E) (e : E) : Set E :=
  {f | ∃ u v, u ≠ v ∧ G.IsLink e u v ∧ G.IsLink f u v}
definitions.notes: The full parallel class of a non-loop edge: all edges with the same unordered, distinct endpoints. Empty on a loop; every use of this definition has the non-loop domain condition.

definitions.name: x2611_15008_seriesClass
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_15008_seriesClass {V E : Type*} (G : Graph V E) (e : E) : Set E :=
  {f | e ∈ G.edgeSet ∧ f ∈ G.edgeSet ∧ ¬ x2611_15008_bridge G e ∧
    ¬ x2611_15008_bridge G f ∧
    (e = f ∨ x2611_15008_components G < x2611_15008_components (G.deleteEdges {e, f}))}
definitions.notes: The full series class of a non-bridge edge: non-bridge edges f equal to e or such that deleting {e,f} increases the component count. With both edges non-bridges and e≠f, this is exactly a two-edge cocircuit. Loops have singleton series classes. Empty outside the non-bridge domain.

definitions.name: x2611_15008_multipleBridge
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_15008_multipleBridge {V E : Type*} (G : Graph V E) (e : E) : Prop :=
  x2611_15008_bridge (G.deleteEdges (x2611_15008_parallelClass G e \ {e})) e
definitions.notes: The paper’s definition: e is a bridge after all other edges in its parallel class have been deleted.

definitions.name: x2611_15008_subdividedLoop
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_15008_subdividedLoop {V E : Type*} (G : Graph V E) (e : E) : Prop :=
  ∃ v, (x2611_15008_contract G (x2611_15008_seriesClass G e \ {e})).IsLoopAt e v
definitions.notes: The paper’s definition: e is a loop after contracting every other edge in its series class.

definitions.name: x2611_15008_Tutte
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_15008_Tutte {V E : Type*} [Fintype E] (G : Graph V E) (x y : ℝ) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact G.edgeSet.toFinset.powerset.sum (fun A =>
    (x - 1) ^ (x2611_15008_components (G.restrict (A : Set E)) - x2611_15008_components G) *
    (y - 1) ^ (A.card + x2611_15008_components (G.restrict (A : Set E)) - G.vertexSet.ncard))
definitions.notes: Real evaluation of the Tutte polynomial by its finite spanning-subgraph expansion: sum over A⊆E(G) of (x−1)^(κ(A)−κ(G)) (y−1)^(|A|+κ(A)−|V(G)|). Edge identities preserve multiple edges; loops contribute to nullity. Graph.restrict retains isolated vertices. For finite graphs both natural exponents are nonnegative, so natural subtraction is exact. No conjecture or lemma from the paper is assumed in this definition.

statements.label: Theorem 2 (loopless inequality)
statements.name: x2611_15008_thm2_loopless
statements.original:
Theorem 2.

Let $a>0,~b>1$ so that $1+ka\leq 2b^{k}$ for all integers $k\geq 1$ and $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges and $\kappa$ connected components. Then

$\displaystyle\frac{T_{G}(1,1)}{T_{G}(2,0)}\leq\frac{b^{m}}{a^{n-\kappa}}$ 
 $\displaystyle\text{if $G$ is loopless, and}$
statements.lean: (V E : Type*) [Fintype V] [Fintype E] (G : Graph V E) (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 1 < b) (hab : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → 1 + (k : ℝ) * a ≤ 2 * b ^ k) (hG : G.Loopless) : x2611_15008_Tutte G 1 1 / x2611_15008_Tutte G 2 0 ≤ b ^ G.edgeSet.ncard / a ^ (G.vertexSet.ncard - x2611_15008_components G)
statements.notes: Finite multigraphs are represented by Mathlib Graph with finite ambient vertex and edge types; every finite multigraph has such a representation. Counts use the actual vertex/edge sets, not the ambient type sizes. First inequality only. The parameter condition over positive natural k is equivalent to the printed condition over integers k≥1. n−κ is a natural exponent. The ratio is real division; no positivity hypothesis for the denominator is added.

fidelity.twin: {V E : Type*} [Fintype E] (G : Graph V E) (hfinite : G.vertexSet.Finite) (n m κ : ℕ) (hn : G.vertexSet.ncard = n) (hm : G.edgeSet.ncard = m) (hκ : x2611_15008_components G = κ) (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 1 < b) (hab : ∀ k : ℤ, 1 ≤ k → 1 + (k : ℝ) * a ≤ 2 * b ^ k) (hloopless : G.Loopless) : x2611_15008_Tutte G 1 1 / x2611_15008_Tutte G 2 0 ≤ b ^ m / a ^ (n - κ)

statements.label: Theorem 2 (bridgeless inequality)
statements.name: x2611_15008_thm2_bridgeless
statements.original:
Theorem 2.

Let $a>0,~b>1$ so that $1+ka\leq 2b^{k}$ for all integers $k\geq 1$ and $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges and $\kappa$ connected components. Then

$\displaystyle\frac{T_{G}(1,1)}{T_{G}(0,2)}\leq\frac{b^{m}}{a^{m-n+\kappa}}$ 
 $\displaystyle\text{if $G$ is bridgeless.}$
statements.lean: (V E : Type*) [Fintype V] [Fintype E] (G : Graph V E) (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 1 < b) (hab : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → 1 + (k : ℝ) * a ≤ 2 * b ^ k) (hG : ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ¬ x2611_15008_bridge G e) : x2611_15008_Tutte G 1 1 / x2611_15008_Tutte G 0 2 ≤ b ^ G.edgeSet.ncard / a ^ (G.edgeSet.ncard + x2611_15008_components G - G.vertexSet.ncard)
statements.notes: Finite multigraphs are represented by Mathlib Graph with finite ambient vertex and edge types; every finite multigraph has such a representation. Counts use the actual vertex/edge sets, not the ambient type sizes. Second inequality only. Bridgeless means that no edge is a bridge; loops are allowed. The exponent m−n+κ is written m+κ−n to avoid an incorrect intermediate truncated subtraction in ℕ. No loopless or connectedness hypothesis is added.

statements.label: Lemma 1(a)–(d)
statements.name: x2611_15008_lemma1
statements.original:
Lemma 1.

([18])
Let $G$ be a graph and $e\in E(G).$ Then:

(a) 

 $T_{G}(x,y)=T_{G-e}(x,y)+T_{G/e}(x,y)$ if $e$ is neither a loop nor a bridge,

(b) 

 $T_{G}(x,y)=xT_{G-e}(x,y)$ if $e$ is a bridge,

(c) 

 $T_{G}(x,y)=yT_{G-e}(x,y)$ if $e$ is a loop.

(d) 

Furthermore, if $G=G_{1}\cup G_{2},$ where $E(G_{1})\cap E(G_{2})=\emptyset$ and $|V(G_{1})\cap V(G_{2})|\leq 1,$ then $T_{G}(x,y)=T_{G_{1}}(x,y)T_{G_{2}}(x,y).$
statements.lean: (V E : Type*) [Fintype V] [Fintype E] (G : Graph V E) (x y : ℝ) : (∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ((¬ (∃ v, G.IsLoopAt e v) ∧ ¬ x2611_15008_bridge G e) → x2611_15008_Tutte G x y = x2611_15008_Tutte (G.deleteEdges {e}) x y + x2611_15008_Tutte (x2611_15008_contract G {e}) x y) ∧ (x2611_15008_bridge G e → x2611_15008_Tutte G x y = x * x2611_15008_Tutte (G.deleteEdges {e}) x y) ∧ ((∃ v, G.IsLoopAt e v) → x2611_15008_Tutte G x y = y * x2611_15008_Tutte (G.deleteEdges {e}) x y)) ∧ (∀ G₁ G₂ : Graph V E, G₁ ≤ G → G₂ ≤ G → G.vertexSet = G₁.vertexSet ∪ G₂.vertexSet → G.edgeSet = G₁.edgeSet ∪ G₂.edgeSet → Disjoint G₁.edgeSet G₂.edgeSet → (G₁.vertexSet ∩ G₂.vertexSet).ncard ≤ 1 → x2611_15008_Tutte G x y = x2611_15008_Tutte G₁ x y * x2611_15008_Tutte G₂ x y)
statements.notes: Finite multigraphs are represented by Mathlib Graph with finite ambient vertex and edge types; every finite multigraph has such a representation. Counts use the actual vertex/edge sets, not the ambient type sizes. All four parts are conjoined. Deletion and contraction are exactly those of the paper; in (b) the factor x multiplies deletion, as printed. In (d), G=G₁∪G₂ is encoded by both subgraph relations and coverage of the vertex and edge sets. The edge sets are disjoint and the vertex intersection has at most one element. Polynomial identities are expressed as equality at every real pair (x,y).

fidelity.twin: {V E : Type*} [Fintype E] (G : Graph V E) (hV : G.vertexSet.Finite) (x y : ℝ) : (∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ((¬ ∃ v, G.IsLoopAt e v) → ¬ x2611_15008_bridge G e → x2611_15008_Tutte G x y = x2611_15008_Tutte (G.deleteEdges {e}) x y + x2611_15008_Tutte (x2611_15008_contract G {e}) x y) ∧ (x2611_15008_bridge G e → x2611_15008_Tutte G x y = x * x2611_15008_Tutte (G.deleteEdges {e}) x y) ∧ ((∃ v, G.IsLoopAt e v) → x2611_15008_Tutte G x y = y * x2611_15008_Tutte (G.deleteEdges {e}) x y)) ∧ (∀ G₁ G₂ : Graph V E, G₁ ≤ G → G₂ ≤ G → G.vertexSet = G₁.vertexSet ∪ G₂.vertexSet → G.edgeSet = G₁.edgeSet ∪ G₂.edgeSet → Disjoint G₁.edgeSet G₂.edgeSet → (G₁.vertexSet ∩ G₂.vertexSet).ncard ≤ 1 → x2611_15008_Tutte G x y = x2611_15008_Tutte G₁ x y * x2611_15008_Tutte G₂ x y)

statements.label: Lemma 4(a)
statements.name: x2611_15008_lemma4_a
statements.original:
Lemma 4.

Let $G$ be a graph, $e\in E(G)$ and $P(e)$ and $S(e)$ be the parallel and series class of $e$ with $|P(e)|=p$ and $|S(e)|=s.$ Then

(a) 

if $P(e)$ is a multiple bridge, then

 $T_{G}(x,y)=xT_{G-P(e)}(x,y)+(y^{p-1}+y^{p-2}+\ldots+y)T_{G/P(e)}(x,y).$
statements.lean: (V E : Type*) [Fintype V] [Fintype E] (G : Graph V E) (e : E) (he : e ∈ G.edgeSet) (hnonloop : ¬ ∃ v, G.IsLoopAt e v) (hnonbridge : ¬ x2611_15008_bridge G e) (p : ℕ) (hp : p = (x2611_15008_parallelClass G e).ncard) (s : ℕ) (hs : s = (x2611_15008_seriesClass G e).ncard) (x y : ℝ) (hcase : x2611_15008_multipleBridge G e) : x2611_15008_Tutte G x y = x * x2611_15008_Tutte (G.deleteEdges (x2611_15008_parallelClass G e)) x y + ((Finset.Ico 1 p).sum (fun i => y ^ i)) * x2611_15008_Tutte (x2611_15008_contract G (x2611_15008_parallelClass G e)) x y
statements.notes: Finite multigraphs are represented by Mathlib Graph with finite ambient vertex and edge types; every finite multigraph has such a representation. Counts use the actual vertex/edge sets, not the ambient type sizes. The descending geometric sum is represented by an ascending finite sum with exactly the same exponents. An empty sum is zero. The identity is evaluated at arbitrary real x,y. Domain ambiguity in the paper: the common introductory hypothesis names both P(e) and S(e), although Section 2 defines the first only for non-loop edges and the second only for non-bridge edges. This literal formalization retains both domain conditions, and both printed cardinality hypotheses |P(e)|=p and |S(e)|=s, even in a subpart using just one class.
